entries.summary: Friday midday confirmed further technology and semiconductor weakness, but the magnitude and direction extend the already material 12:10 ET downside-acceleration assessment rather than establish a distinct new three-day path. Benzinga's 12:15 ET table reports Nasdaq-100 -3.36%, and its 12:43 ET article reports SMH -8.4%, NVDA about -7.3%, AMD -11.7%, MU -12.7%, VIX 30.93. Rates fell as a haven; reported 10Y 4.94% and 2Y 4.65% imply +29 bp, though quote synchronization is not established. Open Watch remains 174 events.

editorial.marketOverview: The midday session continues to show a deep, semiconductor-led Nasdaq drawdown. Benzinga's 12:15 ET index table showed Nasdaq-100 down 3.36%; its 12:43 report described QQQ off about 3.7%, SMH down 8.4%, Nvidia down about 7.3%, AMD 11.7% and Micron 12.7%. VIX was reported at 30.93. The breadth of chip losses makes this more than a single-stock event, though all values remain intraday and not perfectly synchronized.
editorial.whatChanged: Relative to the 12:10 ET assessment, the decline extended modestly, with additional confirmation from the semiconductor ETF and a newly reported midday volatility reading. The earlier assessment had already flagged a material downside acceleration, so this is reinforcement rather than another independent directional regime shift. Curated Open Watch still has 174 events and no newly added catalyst.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The severity of semiconductor ETF underperformance versus QQQ and the broad index suggests AI hardware and duration-sensitive growth remain at the center of deleveraging. A reported VIX above 30 supports heightened risk aversion. Treasuries rallied, with 10Y and 2Y reported at 4.94% and 4.65%; their indicative 29-basis-point positive slope is correctly scaled but not a tick-synchronized rates signal. Michigan inflation expectations eased, a possible medium-term offset to valuation pressure, but did not stop the observed equity selloff.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday afternoon is the first decision point: a close near session lows would strengthen Monday gap-down and continuation risk, while a substantial QQQ-and-semiconductor recovery could favor a volatile oversold bounce. Monday and Tuesday remain bearish-skewed with elevated two-way volatility, not a deterministic decline. The central path has not materially changed since the prior downside-acceleration assessment.
editorial.bullCase: An exhaustion reversal could begin if QQQ recovers with broad participation from SMH and major chip stocks, supported by retreating volatility and falling yields. Defensive-sector strength and softer Michigan inflation expectations provide partial offsets, but without synchronized sector and breadth confirmation they do not establish a durable reversal.
editorial.bearCase: Sustained chip liquidation, VIX above 30 and further negative breadth would make the next two sessions vulnerable to downside follow-through and failed rallies. Continued concerns about AI returns, China chip export controls and tighter Fed expectations remain plausible pressures, but the market response must be distinguished from any unverified incremental catalyst.
editorial.watchNext: Track the 16:00 ET close and next session's QQQ, SOX/SMH, VXN/VIX, advance/decline and yields at comparable timestamps. Verify FedWatch probabilities and next-week scheduled earnings from primary sources. Compare new curated Open Watch events against the unchanged 174-event baseline. Reassess after confirmed closing evidence rather than extrapolating intraday quotes.
